notes: §1985:XII.3.4 GR5 (Amendment 2): "The text produced as a result of the processing of a REPLACE statement must contain neither a COPY statement nor a REPLACE statement." ApplyReplaceStatements screens each whole pseudo-text-2 with ForbiddenIn (REPLACE's rule forbids the words COPY and REPLACE) and ApplyReplacements reports COBOL2574 only when a match actually produces it, at every edition; the witness XREP ==A== BY ==B== draws COBOL2574 at line 8. Probes (classes b, d): an unmatched ==REPLACE== pseudo-text-2 produces nothing and compiles (g5b); a literal "REPLACE COPY" and the word REPLACE-X are not statements and compile (g5c, g5e); a comment and a blank line in pseudo-text-2 compile, as §1985:XII.3.4 GR7 allows (g5d); the word COPY in pseudo-text-2 is a COPY statement processed first (§1985:XII.3.4 GR4), so it is diagnosed as a malformed COPY before REPLACE runs (g5g, g5h).

next.reason: Amendment 2 (X3.23b-1993) changed the rule from 'must not contain a REPLACE statement' to §1985:XII.3.4 GR5 'must contain neither a COPY statement nor a REPLACE statement', so the COPY statement is no longer a 2023 addition. §2023:7.2.4.4 GR9 keeps both and adds three cases: 'shall not contain a COPY statement, a REPLACE statement, a SOURCE FORMAT directive, a comment, or a blank line'. The words that differ are 'a SOURCE FORMAT directive, a comment, or a blank line'. The comment and blank line cases reverse a 1985 result: §1985:XII.3.4 GR7 has 'Comment lines or blank lines in pseudo-text-2 are placed into the resultant program unchanged', where 2023 forbids them in the text REPLACE produces (it removes them in logical conversion, §2023:6.5 GR2 'If the line is a comment line or a blank line, that line is logically discarded').
